title: Throttle visibility explorations + backlog
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for the console pages that make rate limiting, quota consumption, and per-key/per-route usage transparent and actionable for customers. Focus is visibility + remediation flows (quota bump, fallback policies, canary routing).

Audience:
- PMs and designers on Console + Rollouts
- FE engineers implementing telemetry/UI
- Solutions/SEs who need to demo or troubleshoot tenant issues

Goals (what success looks like):
- Customers can quickly see who is being throttled and why (route vs key vs region).
- Provide clear, low-friction remediation actions (request quota bump, increase burst, enable fallback model).
- Surface systemic hotspots (routes that frequently hit limits) so customers can optimize prompts or route traffic.
- Keep the data plane cheap — prefer summaries with drilldowns to raw logs.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Backend provides per-key, per-route time-series of: request counts, token counts, 429/503 counters, and latency percentiles (p50/p95).
- We can query 30d history, but large time-range queries should be sampled/rolled up.
- Must be performant in Console: single-page load should avoid heavy queries; lazy-load detail panels.

Proposed screens (sketch descriptions):
1) Throttle & Quota Overview (top-level)
   - Compact KPI row: active keys (selected org), % keys near quota, 429/min (last 1h), estimated cost impact (est tokens wasted).
   - Alerts strip: red/yellow banners for current rate-limited routes or keys (click to open detail).
   - Timeline sparkline: 1h / 24h / 7d selectable. Hover to show context window with top routes at that time.

2) Heatmap lane: Route x Hour (rolled-up)
   - Visual grid where color intensity = normalized throttle events (429s) per route per hour.
   - Hover shows route name + breakdown (percent 429, avg latency, top keys by volume).
   - Filterable by model family, region, or policy tag (e.g., "production", "staging").

3) Key detail panel (right-side drawer)
   - At-a-glance: key owner, plan tier, hard quota, remaining % for current window, rate-limit policy in effect.
   - Recent incidents list (last 7 days) with one-click: open Jira, open trace in observability, contact SE.
   - Remediation buttons: "Request quota increase" (prepopulated form), "Enable soft-fallback" (toggle to send to cheaper model when near limit), "Create canary" (route copy to test changes).

4) Route drill (per-route page)
   - Long timeline with stacked series: requests, throttles (429), errors, p95 latency.
   - Token efficiency metric: tokens/request vs successful completions.
   - Top offending keys list with proportion and link to key detail.

5) Quota bump flow (UX):
   - Inline form prefilled from selected key/route: current limit, requested limit, reason (free text), expected growth pattern (ramp chart).
   - Triage labels: automated quick-grant for small % increases (<=20%), manual review required for >20% or enterprise plans.
   - Status tracking: form opens a support ticket (Jira-like) and shows ETA.

6) Policy visibility page
   - Show route->policy mapping (rate_limit_policy_id, window size, burst size, enforcement mode).
   - Let admins preview "what-if" traffic: simulate 10k req/min to see expected throttles and fallback triggers.

Wireframe notes (visual behavior):
- Primary interaction is filter + drilldown. Leave most heavy visuals collapsed by default.
- Use banded rows in heatmap to indicate "business critical" routes (user-configured).
- Provide keyboard shortcut to jump to last throttled key/route (power users).
- For time-series, allow sticky vertical cursor showing cross-panel values (so user can correlate an event across overview <-> route drill).

Data / query strategy suggestions:
- Cache 1m aggregates for the last 7d, 5m aggregates for 30d, 1h aggregates for 90d.
- When a drawer opens for a key/route, lazily fetch full 1m data for last 24h only.
- For the heatmap, sample heavy routes and only show top 200 by volume; include an explicit "show more" to avoid overquerying.

A/B experiments to consider:
- Variant A: Inline remediation buttons (request bump, toggle fallback) visible on overview for top-3 hotspots.
- Variant B: Remediation actions hidden behind detail panel to reduce accidental changes.
- Metric: time-to-resolution (from first detection to remediation), ticket conversion rate, support contact reduction.

Accessibility & permissions:
- Only org-admins or key-owners should see quota bump controls.
- Read-only users see all telemetry but mask key IDs (show hash).

Edge cases and notes:
- Keys that are rotated: show canonical mapping for last 30 days to avoid orphaned series.
- Multi-tenant routes: we must avoid exposing other tenants' keys in shared heatmap — show aggregated counts and only list keys when scoped to an org.
- Bursty traffic: alerts should debounce (e.g., 3 mins sustained 429s before banner) to avoid noise.

Open questions (needs product/engineering):
- Can the backend attach "policy id" and "policy type" to each request event? (needed for what-if and mapping).
- Are we able to estimate "wasted tokens" (tokens generated after throttle) efficiently?
- Default thresholds for "near quota" (10%? 20? configurable per plan?)

Backlog grooming list (prioritized):
1) MVP telemetry surfaces: KPI row + timeline + top-10 throttled routes (P0) — owner: Miguel
2) Key detail drawer prototype with actions (P0) — owner: Sanaa
3) Heatmap prototype (sampled routes, 24h) + hover details (P1) — owner: Frontend
4) Quota bump form integration with support flow (automated triage rules) (P1) — owner: Solutions Eng
5) Policy visibility / simulate traffic "what-if" (P2) — owner: Platform Eng
6) A/B experiment infra for remediation visibility (P2) — owner: Growth PM
7) Add tokens-wasted estimate metric and surface it in KPIs (P3) — owner: Observability
8) RBAC gating for controls and key masking for read-only (P1) — owner: SRE

Notes for handoff to designers:
- Please explore a compact card for the KPI row that can be embedded in customer home/dashboard.
- Heatmap should degrade gracefully to list mode on small screens.
- Explore microcopy for "soft fallback": clearly explain expected differences in latency/quality.

Next steps / meetings:
- Sync with Miguel + Sanaa + Omar next Thu (2025-12-04) to lock MVP fields and API contract.
- Add engineering API contract doc to Confluence (link above) and map endpoints to UI components.

Quick links referenced:
- CON-317 (Jira) - console telemetry backlog
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/842 - initial heatmap component
- Confluence: Per-Route Telemetry Spec (linked above)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lightweight; move finalized decisions to the confluence spec and link back.
